question: According to Census of India 2011, what is the gap between male and female literacy rate in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1668**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, the literacy rate among males was **82.14%** and among females was **65.46%**.
 
• The gap between male and female literacy rates is calculated as the difference between these two percentages.
 
• The literacy rate gap is thus **82.14% - 65.46% = 16.68%**.
 
• This percentage gap is equivalent to **0.1668 when expressed as a decimal**, which is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• A census is the procedure of systematically acquiring and recording information about the members of a given population.
 
• It is a regularly occurring and official count of a particular population.
 
• In India, the Census is conducted once every ten years.
 
• The first complete census in India was conducted in 1881.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people who can read and write with understanding in a given population.
 
• It is an important indicator of the educational level of a population.
 
• High literacy rates are often associated with higher levels of economic development.
 
 
 
• **Gender Disparity in Literacy**
 
 
• Gender disparity in literacy refers to the difference in literacy rates between males and females.
 
• This disparity is often a result of socio-cultural factors that prioritize male education over female education.
 
• Reducing this gap is crucial for achieving gender equality and empowering women.
